# Exactly-once guarantee with UUIDv5, advisory lock, and existence check

> A deterministic UUIDv5 `journalId`, PostgreSQL advisory lock, and transaction-scoped existence check ensure settlement journals post exactly once despite Kafka redeliveries.

_Part of [Settling paid orders to shops](settling-orders-to-shops.md)_

This is the mechanism that ensures a settlement journal posts exactly once, even if Kafka redelivers the same `order.paid` event multiple times. It lives in the [`SettlementListener`](settling-orders-to-shops.md), which reacts to each order payment and must record how the net amount (total minus platform fee) is split among the shops in that order. To make settlement idempotent, the listener generates a deterministic `journalId` using UUIDv5 of the order ID and a fixed namespace—the same order ID always produces the same `journalId`, even on retries. Then it runs a database transaction that acquires a PostgreSQL advisory lock on the `journalId` hash (serializing concurrent attempts), checks if any [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) with that `journalId` already exists (if so, skips), and otherwise calls [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md) to post the journal. The combination of advisory lock and existence check in the same transaction guarantees exactly-once semantics: the first attempt posts the `journalId`; any concurrent or retried attempt finds it locked or finds the existing entry and skips.

**Look at:** [`SettlementListener` in settlement.listener.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/settlement.listener.ts#L23)

## Pieces

- Fixed UUID namespace constant for deterministic journalIds: The constant `SETTLEMENT_NS` is combined with the order ID via UUIDv5 to generate an idempotent `journalId`: the same order ID always produces the same ID, enabling retries to recognize and skip already-posted settlements.
- [PostgreSQL advisory lock to serialize concurrent attempts](settlement-advisory-lock.md): `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(journalId))` acquires a transaction-scoped lock on the `journalId` hash, blocking concurrent transactions from processing the same settlement simultaneously.
- Existence check to detect already-posted settlements: A `SELECT EXISTS` query inside the transaction checks if [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) already contains an entry with the `journalId`; if it does, the settlement is skipped because it was already posted.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| event | `order.paid` | Consumed by [`SettlementListener`](settling-orders-to-shops.md). The event payload includes order ID, total amount, platform fee, shop lines, and payment ID. |
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | Existence check reads this table by `journalId` to detect if settlement was already posted. Settlement inserts new entries via `LedgerService.post()`. |
| event | `ledger.journal_posted` | Published via outbox when the settlement journal is posted, emitted as part of `LedgerService.post()` in the same transaction. |

## Watch out

- `SETTLEMENT_NS` is hardcoded; changing it would create new `journalIds` for all existing orders and break idempotency.
- The advisory lock is transaction-scoped; it is released when the transaction commits or rolls back, not held beyond the request.
- The existence check must run inside the same transaction as the lock; running them separately allows a concurrent transaction to slip in and post a duplicate.
- Shops are sorted alphabetically before allocation; this must be deterministic, or different processes might allocate shares differently to the same settlement.
